I was not able to locate a definitive list of the species that fall under the subfamily Phyllostominae that were recorded during the 2022 Rapid Assessment Program (RAP) expedition to Alto Mayo. The RAP release that covers the Alto Mayo region is titled **“Rapid Assessment Program Bulletin of Biological Assessment 73.”**  The PDF is referenced on Conservation International’s website (https://www.conservation.org/sites/default/files/RAP_Bulletin_of_Biological_Assessment_73.pdf) and is almost 500 pages long, but I have not accessed or examined its contents to extract the specific bat species.  

Because I have not retrieved the text of that bulletin, I cannot provide the comprehensive list of Phyllostominae species documented by the expedition.  If you need that information you would need to obtain and review the PDF, which should contain the full taxonomic inventory for the region, including all recorded Phyllostominae bats.
